title: Fix AtomicWriteFile with an Open reader on Windows
body:
On Windows, AtomicWriteFile fails with "Access is denied" when another process has the destination file open. For example, `podman machine start`, fails to update the machine config while `podman machine list` is reading it [1].

The problem is that, on Windows, Go `os.Rename` uses the Win32 API `MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` [2] that fails if the destination files has an open handle, even if it has been opened with the flag `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` [3].

To address that we have implemented a POSIX rename function that calls `CreateFile` [4], to open the temporary file, and then `SetInformationByHandle` [5], with flags `FILE_RENAME_POSIX_SEMANTICS` and `FILE_RENAME_REPLACE_IF_EXISTS` [6], to rename the file.

Note that, in this case, replacing the file still needs a DELETE access to it, so readers must have opened it with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`.

We are still using Go `os.Rename` though, and fall back to `posixRename` only if the first fails. This has two benefits:
- `MoveFileEx` is more portable compared to `SetInformationByHandle`, it is supported on older versions of Windows.
- If another process holds an exclusive delete access handle, trying it a second time, gives us a chance that the handle has been released and renaming succeeds.

This commits doesn't fix [1] completely, because `podman machine ls` still reads the configuration file without the `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` flag. But it mitigates it, because of the retry. Another commit, Podman side, is needed to fix it definitely.

[1] https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28873
[2] https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.0/src/internal/syscall/windows/syscall_windows.go
[3] https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-movefileexw
[4] https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilew
[5] https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-setfileinformationbyhandle
[6] https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/ns-ntifs-_file_rename_information
